body.v: Your October statement is attached. Please open the attachment and sign in to view the details.
If you have questions, just reply to this email.

hotspots.explain: This address looks right, but a sender address can be forged. Check where a reply would go.
Replies would go to swissalpbank-mail.example, a different domain from the bank's. That mismatch is a classic trick.
"statement-october.pdf.html" ends in .html: it is a web page dressed up as a PDF. It would show you a fake sign-in.
Your first name is easy to find. It does not prove who wrote the email.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Not the bank, despite the sender address. The reply-to is on swissalpbank-mail.example, so any answer would go to someone else.
choices: Someone faking the bank's address, with replies going elsewhere

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Only mild curiosity: it is an ordinary-looking statement, which is the point. Nothing here is pushing you.
choices: Mild curiosity: it looks like routine mail

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the attachment and sign in. The attachment is a web page that would collect your login.
choices: Open the attachment and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not open it. Look for your statement in the SwissAlpBank app, or call the number on your card.
choices: Open the attachment to check it
Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself to see your statements
Reply and ask if it is genuine

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and look under Documents
actions.consequence: Your statement is there, or not yet. Either way you never touched the attachment.

actions.label: Open the attachment to see the statement
actions.consequence: A fake sign-in page opens. If you type your login, it goes to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply and ask whether the statement is genuine
actions.consequence: Your reply goes to the scammer's address, not the bank. They tell you it is genuine.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it

attacker_reveal: The sender looked right, so you stopped checking... but I made your replies come to me, and the "PDF" was a web page with a mask on. Always read to the very end of a file name.
